subject.title: Memory MVP: build write pipeline with classification, dedupe, merge, and conflict handling

question: Should the Memory MVP write resolver be owned by memory-core as the active-memory write contract, by Memory Wiki as the knowledge-layer workflow, or by a new plugin/SDK seam before implementation starts?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the request defines durable memory schema, conflict policy, provenance semantics, and operator UX that automation cannot safely choose from code alone.

options.title: Design memory-core resolver contract first
options.body: Use memory-core as the owning contract for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history, with Memory Wiki consuming the settled model.

options.title: Route through Memory Wiki
options.body: Treat contradictions, claims, and source evidence as Memory Wiki responsibilities and keep memory-core as Markdown/search/promotion until a lower-level write API is needed.

options.title: Defer the resolver
options.body: Keep current Markdown, promotion, and wiki layers while collecting more production examples before accepting durable schema or UX commitments.

recommendation.title: Design memory-core resolver contract first
recommendation.body: Use memory-core as the owning contract for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history, with Memory Wiki consuming the settled model.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about memory/plugin product boundaries, and steipete has the strongest sampled history around Memory Wiki docs and VISION.md direction.
